claims.text: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi exhibits a marked change in plastic deformation behavior with temperature.
The temperature dependence of plastic deformation in CoCrFeMnNi is caused by changes in dislocation mobility.
The temperature dependence of plastic deformation in CoCrFeMnNi is associated with changes in microstructural stability.
The initial equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi alloy has a homogeneous, undeformed microstructure.
Temperature changes alter dislocation interactions in equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Dynamic strain aging may occur as temperature changes in equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Temperature may change ordering or precipitate stability in equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
At lower temperatures, limited thermal activation constrains dislocation motion in equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Constrained dislocation motion at lower temperatures produces higher yield strength.
At elevated temperatures, enhanced thermal activation increases dislocation mobility in equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Elevated temperature may promote dynamic recovery in equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Increasing temperature from ambient toward 900 °C will reduce the yield strength of equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Increasing temperature from ambient toward 900 °C will increase the ductility of equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
The temperature-dependent mechanical transition will be accompanied by altered dislocation density and interaction patterns.
Different alloy-processing histories or compositions may change the observed temperature-dependent behavior.
